chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Al-Hisham ibn Salim from 'Ammar al-Sabati who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a boy who was nursed by a woman: is it permissible for him to marry her sister by the father through nursing? He said: No, for they have all been nursed from the milk of one single bull from one woman. I said: Does he marry her sister by the mother through nursing? He said: There is no harm in that, for her sister who did not nurse him, her bull was different from the bull of the one who nursed the boy, so the two bulls differed, so there is no harm.

key_terms.فَحْل: Bull (used here to denote the source of milk in the context of the ruling)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Can a man marry the sister of his wet nurse if they were nursed by different women?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar elucidates the Shia juristic principle that milk kinship (radāʿah) is established through both the nursing woman and the bull whose milk she consumed, a nuance distinguishing it from some Sunni schools. It clarifies that marriage is prohibited with the sister of the nursing woman if they share the same nursing source (one woman and one bull), but permitted if the sister was nursed by a different woman and thus a different bull, highlighting the importance of tracing the biological source of the milk. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the dual lineage of milk—maternal and paternal—when determining mahram relationships.
